title: Radio: 2-Sam-14, Stalled Hay Truck at Highway 305 Canyon Mouth

lines.text: I've got a stalled flatbed hay truck at the Highway 305 canyon mouth, westbound lane, about a hundred yards above the mile marker pullout. Driver says the fuel pump died. A tow out of the plains is 40 minutes. I'll hold here and run one lane, but that takes me off the Gulch Road patrol. Do you want CDOT notified?
Copy, 2-Sam-14. Stalled flatbed, Highway 305 canyon mouth, westbound, one lane, tow 40 minutes out. Stand by.
2-Sam-14 copies. Lights are on and cones are out. Traffic's light right now, but it'll pick up when the school buses start rolling.

fields.voiceStyle: Male deputy in his thirties, flat and routine, patrol car idling, wind gusting past the open window; the dispatcher is a calm female voice in her forties.

instructorNote: This is a noise inject. Watch for Dispatch to log it as a traffic incident, notify CDOT because Highway 305 is a state highway, and post the road as Controlled with a time on the hourly shared road status list (SENTCS 5). Also watch for the Sheriff to get the deputy back to the Gulch Road patrol quickly, without treating a mechanical breakdown as a fire-weather event.
